title: The Lion and the Mouse
blurb: A mouse wakes a sleeping lion. Later, the lion needs her.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… on a wide golden plain where the grass grew taller than a man, there slept a Lion. [gently] He was the biggest creature for miles and miles. When he breathed, the grass bent. When he yawned, the birds went quiet.

[softly] And on this warm afternoon, he was fast asleep in the shade.

[playfully] Now a little Mouse came hurrying through the grass. She was in a great rush, the way small creatures often are… and she was not looking where she was going.

[surprised] She ran straight up over something warm. Something soft. Something that rose… and fell… and rose again.

[whispers] It was the Lion's paw.

[loudly] The Lion's eyes opened. His great paw closed around her.

[grandly] “Who,” he rumbled, “is running about on ME?”

[worried] The Mouse trembled. “I am sorry! I am so sorry. I did not see you. Please let me go — [short pause] and one day, perhaps, I shall help YOU.”

[laughs] Well. The Lion laughed. He laughed until the birds flew up out of the trees.

[amused] “You?” he said. “Help ME? You are the size of my whisker.”

[gently] But he was a Lion in a good mood, and it was a warm afternoon… so he opened his paw. [softly] “Go on, little one.”

[excited] And the Mouse ran, and ran, and ran.

[calmly] Many days passed. The rains came and went. The grass grew taller still.

[worried] And then one evening, hunters came across the plain. They spread a great rope net between the trees… and in the dark, the Lion walked into it.

[firmly] He pulled. He twisted. He pushed with all his enormous strength. [sad] But the more he fought, the tighter the ropes held him.

The Lion roared. It was a terrible sound, and it rolled out across the whole plain, all the way to a small hole under a root… [curious] where a little Mouse lifted her head and listened.

[excited] “I know that voice,” she said. And she ran towards it.

[softly] She found him tangled and still. “Be quiet now,” she said. “And keep still.”

[calmly] Then she began to bite. One rope. Then another. Her small sharp teeth went snip… snip… snip… all through the night.

[warmly] And when the sun came up, the net fell away, and the Lion stood free.

[gently] “You were right,” he said softly. “Even the smallest friend can be the one you need.”
